title: U.S. Senate · Montana

context.text: This is an open seat. On March 4, 2026, incumbent Sen. Steve Daines (R) withdrew his candidacy and endorsed Kurt Alme, who filed to run the same day; Seth Bodnar also filed as an independent that day. According to Montana Free Press, this makes the race the first Montana U.S. Senate election without an incumbent running in 40 years. Alme, Alani Bankhead and Bodnar are viewed as the leading candidates. On July 8, 2026, 17 Democratic state legislators publicly asked Bankhead and Bodnar to decide which of them would end their campaign, warning a split vote could help Republicans; neither withdrew, and the deadline to withdraw from the ballot passed on August 10, 2026, so both remain on the ballot.

candidates.name: Kurt Alme
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the Republican primary on June 2, 2026; entered the race March 4, 2026 after Sen. Steve Daines withdrew and endorsed him.
candidates.currentRole: Former U.S. Attorney for the District of Montana (Oct. 2025–March 2026)

summary.text: Kurt Alme is the Republican nominee for the open U.S. Senate seat. A Montana native and attorney, he has worked in private practice, as director of the state Department of Revenue, as state budget director and as U.S. Attorney for Montana, and says he has never run for office before. He entered the race on March 4, 2026, when Sen. Steve Daines withdrew and endorsed him.

background.text: Born October 7, 1966, in Great Falls, Montana, to two educators; the family lived in Dillon, Victor and Helena before settling in Miles City, where he graduated from Custer County District High School.

Earned a bachelor's degree in business from the University of Colorado and a law degree from Harvard Law School. His campaign says he graduated summa cum laude and was a Truman Scholar at Colorado, and graduated cum laude from Harvard.
Clerked for U.S. District Judge Charles Lovell in Helena, then practiced at the Crowley Fleck law firm in Billings, where he became a partner.
Served as director of the Montana Department of Revenue under Gov. Judy Martz (R); his campaign says he led a cut to the state's top income tax rate.
Served as an Assistant U.S. Attorney for Montana from 2003 to 2010 and as First Assistant U.S. Attorney from 2006 to 2010, according to Wikipedia.
Was president and general counsel of the Yellowstone Boys and Girls Ranch Foundation, and, according to his campaign, an executive with the National Christian Foundation.
Nominated by President Trump and confirmed as U.S. Attorney for the District of Montana in 2017, serving until December 2020; he served as state budget director under Gov. Greg Gianforte (R) in 2021.

Returned as U.S. Attorney in 2025 and left the post on March 4, 2026, to run for Senate. Ballotpedia and Wikipedia give different start dates for this second term (October 7, 2025 and March 17, 2025).
According to his campaign website, he lives in Billings with his wife Sandra, and they have two grown children.

priorities.text: Says he is running to protect veterans, defend the Second Amendment, keep transgender girls and women out of women's and girls' sports, support farmers and ranchers, protect public lands, and secure elections.

candidates.name: Alani Bankhead
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the Democratic primary on June 2, 2026.

summary.text: Alani Bankhead is the Democratic nominee for the open U.S. Senate seat. She is a retired U.S. Air Force lieutenant colonel and former federal supervisory special agent who describes a career in counterintelligence, protective operations and child-exploitation investigations. She is a first-time candidate, running on affordability, accountability and protecting vulnerable people.

background.text: According to her campaign website, she grew up moving frequently as the child of a military parent, and later chose to settle in Montana.
Earned a bachelor's degree in criminal justice and Latin American studies from Pennsylvania State University in 2004 and a graduate degree from Troy University in 2012.

Served 21 years in the U.S. Air Force, retiring as a lieutenant colonel. Her campaign says her work included human-intelligence operations in Iraq, arresting child predators in Japan, commanding a unit in Kuwait, and serving as head bodyguard to a senior Pentagon official.

According to her campaign press kit, as senior bodyguard to the Secretary of the Air Force she led more than 200 agents on 700 protective missions, and she led an FBI and Defense Department counterintelligence task force.

After active duty, led Latin American investigations and law-enforcement training for an international anti-slavery organization and, her campaign says, helped build Operation Keiki Shield in Hawai'i, a multi-agency effort against child exploitation.
Became a certified professional coach and founded Mighty Sparrow Coaching.
Describes Montana as the first home she chose rather than one assigned by military service.

priorities.text: Running on housing, healthcare, and government accountability.
"After 21 years of serving, I was looking at my beautiful state and country burning and I knew I had a special set of skills to offer the people of Montana."

candidates.name: Seth Bodnar
candidates.ballotNote: Filed as an independent on March 4, 2026, the same day Sen. Steve Daines withdrew.
candidates.currentRole: Former president of the University of Montana

summary.text: Seth Bodnar is an independent candidate for the open U.S. Senate seat. A West Point graduate, Rhodes Scholar and Army Special Forces officer, he became a General Electric executive and then served as president of the University of Montana from 2018 until he resigned in January 2026. He entered the race on March 4, 2026, running as an independent who says he will not caucus with either party.

background.text: Raised in Franklin, Pennsylvania, the son of two public school teachers.

Graduated first in his class from the U.S. Military Academy at West Point with a bachelor's degree in economics, then studied at Hertford College, Oxford, as a Rhodes Scholar and Truman Scholar, earning two master's degrees.

Served in the U.S. Army as an infantry officer in the 101st Airborne Division, deployed to Iraq, and served as a Green Beret in the 1st Special Forces Group, commanding a detachment; he later taught economics at West Point. He remained a lieutenant colonel in the Montana Army National Guard as of 2022.
Joined General Electric in 2011 and became a senior executive in its transportation division, including as chief digital officer.

Became the 19th president of the University of Montana in January 2018. According to his campaign, enrollment was turned around, finances stabilized and research output doubled; the university also settled a sex-discrimination lawsuit for $350,000 in 2024 that named him, according to Wikipedia.
Resigned as university president in January 2026 and announced his Senate run on March 4, 2026. Wikipedia reports he was last registered with a party in 2012, as a Democrat.
According to his campaign, his wife is a pediatrician and they are raising three children; Wikipedia lists the family's residence as Missoula.

priorities.text: "This country is in crisis, and our national political parties are failing us. Montanans are an independent people, and they deserve an independent voice fighting for them in Washington, DC. I'm not a politician, I'm a soldier, a businessman, a husband, a father."

candidates.name: Kyle Austin
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the Libertarian Party primary on June 2, 2026; previously a Libertarian candidate in 2022 and 2024.

summary.text: Kyle Austin is the Libertarian nominee for the open U.S. Senate seat. A Havre-raised pharmacist, farmer and owner of the pharmacy company Pharm406, he previously ran for Montana's eastern U.S. House seat as a Republican in 2022 and 2024. He says he is running on health-care overhaul, agriculture and smaller government.

background.text: Born in Havre, Montana, on the Hi-Line, and raised partly on his grandfather's farm; graduated from Havre High School in 2001.
Earned a doctorate in pharmacy from the University of Montana Pharmacy School in 2008.

Worked as a pharmacist for about 18 years, according to his own account, including traveling the state doing pharmacy work before founding Pharm406, an independent pharmacy based in Billings with an office in Butte.
Owns family farmland west of Havre where he has grown wheat, barley and canola; describes himself as a fourth-generation Montanan, farmer, pilot and small-business owner.

Ran for Montana's 2nd Congressional District seat as a Republican in 2022 and 2024, and says he switched to the Libertarian Party because he considers both major parties dysfunctional; he won the 2026 Libertarian nomination in the June primary.

researchNotes: Basic-tier research relying primarily on Ballotpedia's race and candidate biography pages, as no incumbent is running and no personal campaign websites were consulted in the time available. Write-in candidate Jami Woodman was excluded. Alme's U.S. Attorney tenure dates differ between Ballotpedia and Wikipedia; the biography states both. Austin's House runs in 2022 and 2024 come from news reports; the Montana Libertarian Party had endorsed a different primary candidate, which is omitted here.
